wacc.formula: WACC = wₑ × kₑ + w_d × k_d × (1 − t);  kₑ = r_f + β × ERP

methods.formula: Value per share = (peer median EV/Sales × Revenue − net debt) ÷ shares
methods.fit: It has revenue ($29.21B over four quarters) — the measure that still works without profit, and 7 peers (SIC 4833) have the multiple.

methods.formula: Value = book + Σ (ROEₜ − kₑ) × Bookₜ₋₁ ÷ (1 + kₑ)ᵗ over 10 years; ROE fades linearly to kₑ; half of earnings retained
inputs: SEC 10-K / 10-Q, trailing four quarters: pretax income − income tax (the main site's reading)
methods.fit: Equity is positive ($11.77B) and so is net income (−$5.87B), so the return it earns on book value can be compared with what shareholders require.

methods.formula: Value per share = (1 − p) × going-concern value + p × liquidation value
inputs: SEC filing cover page: shares outstanding (after a split or issue)
assumptions: one-year distress: the blended Merton / CDS / Altman / cushion estimate (credit panel)
an assumption for a forced sale
methods.fit: It is burning cash (free cash flow −$5.14B a year, a runway of 0.5 years), so its value must allow for the chance it does not survive.

methods.formula: Stage-weighted value = Σ weight × central value of the stage's methods (weights renormalized over the methods available)
assumptions: fixed by stage before any result was seen (base_rates.STAGES)
methods.fit: Its stage is “Decline / turnaround” — operating income ≤ 0, revenue growth unknown — which fixes these methods and their weights in advance.

methods.formula: Value = D₀ × [(1 + g_L) + H × (g_S − g_L)] ÷ (kₑ − g_L);  growth falls in a straight line from g_S to g_L over 2H years
inputs: SEC filing cover page: shares outstanding (after a split or issue)
assumptions: an assumption: dividends rarely grow faster for a decade
methods.fit: It pays a dividend whose growth is likely to slow from today's pace to the economy's, which the H-model spreads over ten years.
